reasoning: The claim oversimplifies and distorts the findings of a widely cited March 2023 Goldman Sachs economics report. The study estimated that generative AI could expose roughly 300 million full-time jobs worldwide to automation or replace the equivalent workload of tasks. However, the report explicitly emphasized that exposure does not equate to outright job elimination; for most workers and industries, generative AI is expected to complement human labor rather than fully replace it, alongside creating new roles and boosting global productivity. Presenting this figure as a definitive prediction that 300 million jobs "will be replaced" strips essential nuance from the projection.
